name: sarcasm
quote: That's a top-performing organization, I tell you.
description: A statement that is intended to mean the opposite of the literal meaning, signaling negativity about something with attempted humor.
perceptions: Saying the negative thing I want to say in a direct way would sound boring or be ineffective.
Perhaps others would appreciate if I made the comment in an indirect way.
Perhaps the target of the barb will find the comment witty.
results: Some people find sarcasm amusing and witty if done well. Others do not.

guidance.description: If that’s what sarcasm looks like, I don’t want any part of it. 10 reasons to put the sarcasm aside.
How to Enhance Your Sarcasm Skills

variations.name: perceived sarcasm
variations.description: Detecting sarcasm involves physical perceptions like tone of voice, comparing the literal meaning of words within their context, and perhaps knowing something of the speaker's habits and beliefs.
perceptions: Someone said something that doesn't make sense if taken literally.
results: You may react to perceived sarcasm with experiences including humor, annoyance, contempt, or anger depending on the context and perceptions about the speakers intentions.

guidance.description: Sarcastic people can be hilarious. But when their barbs are pointed at you, they can be annoying or even hurtful. Here's how to deal.

comparisons.description: Sarcasm and irony both point out something that's the opposite of what's expected, but sarcasm always carries a negative editorial message.

commentaries.quote: Sarcasm is verbal irony that carries a negative message.
Sarcasm helps me overcome the harshness of the reality we live, eases the pain of scars and makes people smile.
Sarcasm I now see to be, in general, the language of the Devil; for which reason I have, long since, as good as renounced it.
The subconscious doesn't distinguish sarcasm and jokes. It just accepts what it hears. That's the power of words.
Enjoyment of sarcasm may be driven by a sense of disappointment with the world, boredom, and/or the novelty perceived from a witty statement.
